purpose: Checks a book of event-contract positions, stated as quantities and prices only, against caller-declared position accountability levels and position limits, per contract, per event or per series: computes each position maximum loss from the side (yes loses its full cost, no loses payout minus price), rounded up to the next minor unit (ceiling, conservative toward finding); nets yes and no quantities on the same contract only when the caller declares per_contract_net; applies market-maker treatment as data (accountability multiplier default 10x and limit exemption on program contracts under the pinned Kalshi rulebook profile, all values caller-overridable, no defaults on the generic profile); and reports accountability breaches and limit breaches each with the profile rule cite, verdict WITHIN, ACCOUNTABILITY_REVIEW or LIMIT_BREACH. Every limit figure is caller-supplied -- the node hard-codes no venue figure -- and aggregation across similar contracts is venue-specific: CFTC staff guidance on that question (staff advisory and advance notice, 2026) sets no numeric levels. Under per_contract_net the node refuses (CROSS_EVENT_LABEL_REFUSED under per_event, CROSS_SERIES_LABEL_REFUSED under per_series) when a single contract's legs disagree on the label its aggregation groups by, rather than inherit the first leg's label; this is order-independent and invents no convention the venue rulebook does not state, so callers must split or relabel such books. The node reports arithmetic against declared levels; it never states that a participant violated a rule. Declared domain exclusions: identifier-like labels (account ids, member ids, addresses, emails, hashes) are refused and never echoed; unknown profiles, malformed dates, out-of-window as_of, out-of-enum aggregation, netting, participant class, side and limit basis are refused with structured non-verdicts; no fee or pricing arithmetic (fee and pricing nodes art-211 and art-212 cover that); no trading or legal advice.
